prompt.context: Uranus Co., founded in 1969 by Jack Kanof, is an established aerospace company looking to penetrate the luxury space travel market. It is looking for advice on the global launch of its new travel service, which will be a 2-week cruise experience on a spaceship orbiting earth. Uranus is trying to determine whether they should enter the market and if they can be profitable.
prompt.question: How would you advise Uranus Co.?

clarifying_info.q: What is Uranus Co.'s current business model?
clarifying_info.a: Uranus works with both governments and other private companies to provide aerospace equipment and assets.

clarifying_info.q: Who are Uranus Co.'s main competitors?
clarifying_info.a: SpaceX and MoonShine are Uranus's biggest competitors.
Uranus Co. wants to assess whether the space travel market is lucrative and large enough to enter. They also want to breakeven in 2 years.
Uranus Co. operates globally and is headquartered in Bangkok.

clarifying_info.q: What is the product or service like?
clarifying_info.a: Similar to a cruise ship experience — a 2-week voyage orbiting earth.

exhibits.title: Market Research
exhibits.shows: A table of global and survey-based market research metrics for potential space travel customers, including global population, millionaire percentage, age and location breakdowns, a survey of 200 American millionaires on travel interest and ticket purchasing intent, and health condition data.

data.Travel requirement: Must not have any heart conditions

exhibits.title: Competitive Landscape
exhibits.shows: A pie chart of current market share by number of tickets (SpaceX 50%, MoonShine 30%, Rest of Market 20% with no single player above 6%), and a radar/spider chart comparing SpaceX, MoonShine, and Uranus across five dimensions: Cost, Distance from Earth, Length of Voyage, Amenities, and Safety.

data.Dimensions compared: Cost, Distance from Earth, Length of Voyage, Amenities, Safety
data.Note: Shorter bar on spider chart indicates higher cost

exhibits.title: Customer Surveys
exhibits.shows: A radar chart showing customer importance ratings across five dimensions (Cost, Distance from Earth, Length of Trip, Amenities, Safety), accompanied by three customer quotes reflecting their preferences.

data.Dimensions rated: Cost, Distance from Earth, Length of Trip, Amenities, Safety
data.Quote 1: I want the voyage to be longer so I can relax and get my money's worth.
data.Quote 2: The higher we are, the better the view. We should be as high as possible.
data.Quote 3: Cost does not matter to me. I'll pay extra for the best experience.

exhibits.title: Operations Information
exhibits.shows: A table of key operational metrics for Uranus Co.'s fleet and launch infrastructure.

exhibits.title: Revenue and Cost Data
exhibits.shows: A table of revenue per customer and fixed/variable cost details for Uranus Co.'s space travel service.

framework: Revenues: Tickets, Food/Drinks/Merchandise, Onboard Activities, Broadcasting (Live Stream)
Costs — Fixed: Spaceships, Marketing, Insurance, Launch Pad Permit/Lease; Variable: Fuel, Maintenance, Food/Drink and Activities, Wages
Internal capabilities: IP, Operational capabilities, Financial capacity, Brand Image
Market: Competition (strengths/weaknesses, market shares), Customers (demographics, preferences)
Regulatory environment: Product, Price, Length of trip, Safety, Onboard experiences
Go-to-Market strategy: Organic growth, Partnerships, M&A

questions.prompt: What factors would you consider in estimating the market size for this service?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify: Global population, % that are millionaires, health/age eligibility requirements for space travel, willingness to travel to space, and average number of tickets per traveler (family size). Red herrings in Exhibit 1 are asthma, age over 50, and living in a city — the only health requirement is no heart conditions.

questions.prompt: Using the market research data in Exhibit 1, estimate the total market size of space travel tickets.
questions.guidance: Strong candidate filters out red herrings (asthma, age 50+, city residence), applies only the heart-condition filter, combines Yes and Maybe survey responses as part of the addressable market, and multiplies by average ticket purchases. A great candidate notes the survey sample bias (only American millionaires, self-reported health).

math.setup: Start with global millionaires, apply only the heart-condition eligibility filter (3/8 have heart conditions so 5/8 are eligible), then apply willingness-to-travel rate, then multiply by average tickets per person per year.
steps: Willing to travel (Yes + Maybe): 5M x (90+30)/200 = 5M x 120/200 = 5M x 60% = 3M
Total tickets per year: 3M x 2.3 = 6.9M tickets

questions.prompt: How much of the market do you think Uranus can penetrate? Use Exhibits 2 and 3 to support your estimate.
questions.guidance: A good candidate notes the market is fragmented outside the top two players (20% split among many small players) and that Uranus leads on nearly all metrics except cost — but Exhibit 3 shows customers don't care much about cost. Therefore Uranus is well-positioned to capture the fragmented 20% immediately and gradually siphon share from SpaceX and MoonShine. A great candidate notes that share capture from the top two will be gradual as Uranus must first prove itself. Allow candidate to propose their own estimate before revealing Uranus's internal target of 20%.

questions.prompt: Uranus Co. wants to penetrate at least 20% of the market each year. Using Exhibits 4 and 5, does Uranus have the operational capacity to meet this 20% target?
questions.guidance: Candidate multiplies trips per month by months by ships to get annual trips, then multiplies by ship capacity to get annual ticket capacity, and compares to 20% of total market (6.9M x 20% = 1.38M). Should conclude capacity slightly exceeds target.

math.setup: Calculate annual ticket capacity from fleet size, trip frequency, and ship capacity.
steps: Annual trips: 2 trips/ship/month x 12 months x 150 ships = 3,600 trips/year
Annual ticket capacity: 400 passengers/trip x 3,600 trips = 1,440,000 tickets/year
math.answer: Yes — Uranus can handle 1.44M tickets/year, which is 20.87% of the 6.9M ticket market, just above the 20% target.

questions.prompt: If Uranus runs at full capacity, will it be able to break even within two years?
questions.guidance: Candidate must calculate startup cost (build all ships), annual fixed costs (fuel, maintenance, launch pads, insurance, payroll, marketing), contribution margin per customer (revenue minus variable cost), and then solve for breakeven years. Strong candidate correctly identifies ship construction as a one-time upfront cost separate from annual fixed costs.

math.setup: Startup cost = ship build cost x fleet size. Annual fixed costs = fuel + maintenance + launch pad leases + other fixed. Contribution margin = revenue per customer - variable cost per customer. Breakeven: Startup cost = (CM x tickets/year - annual fixed costs) x years.
steps: Annual fuel cost: 500,000 gal/trip x 3,600 trips x $5/gal = $9B
Annual launch pad leases: 10 pads x $10M = $100M
Other fixed costs: $450M insurance + $40M payroll + $50M marketing = $540M
Contribution margin: $500k - $400k variable cost = $100k per customer
math.answer: Uranus Co. breaks even in approximately 1.68 years — within the 2-year target.

brainstorming.prompt: What risks or concerns should Uranus Co. consider before entering this market?

categories.name: Regulatory
ideas: Space travel regulations could change with little notice
International regulatory differences across Uranus's global operations

categories.name: Safety and Liability
ideas: Human safety in orbit is a significant liability exposure
Insurance costs could rise sharply after any incident
Reputational risk from a single high-profile accident

categories.name: Market and Data Quality
ideas: Survey sample is only 200 American millionaires — not globally representative
Demand estimates could be overstated or understated

categories.name: Competitive and Operational
ideas: SpaceX and MoonShine will respond to market entry
Setup time and complexity of building 150 ships before launch
Competitor actions during the multi-year construction period
Supply chain and skilled labor constraints for ship construction

recommendation: Uranus Co. should enter the luxury space travel market
The market is sizable (~6.9M tickets/year) and Uranus's capabilities — superior distance, voyage length, amenities, and safety — position it strongly against fragmented competitors
Financial projections show breakeven in ~1.68 years at full capacity, comfortably within the 2-year target
Uranus's existing aerospace expertise provides a meaningful competitive moat
risks: Regulatory risks could change on short notice
Safety and liability concerns are an important consideration
Current survey data has a small sample size and may not be fully representative of the global population
Setup time and competitor actions during the construction phase could erode first-mover advantage
next_steps: Conduct additional global market surveys (beyond American millionaires) to better validate demand
Begin hiring pilots, flight attendants, maintenance staff, and construction personnel to build out the workforce and start ship construction
Launch a marketing blitz and begin taking pre-orders in preparation for the maiden voyage
